newsitem.title: USA: Radio Free Asia broadcasts said jammed to Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Radio Free Asia broadcasts said jammed to Vietnam.

text.p: The first broadcasts on Thursday of Radio Free Asia to Vietnam appear to have been jammed, the U.S.-backed radio station said.
Radio Free Asia, which broadcasts from Washington to several Asian countries, said international monitoring stations in nearby nations had detected the jamming.

"Despite the jamming, the RFA signal could still be heard in some locations in Vietnam, indicating that the station's programming was not being totally obliterated," said Radio Free Asia president Richard Richte, citing phone calls to listeners in Vietnam.
Hanoi last week said it would step up internal vigilance and increase domestic propaganda in response to plans by Radio Free Asia to begin broadcasts to Vietnam.

A commentary in the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper described the U.S.-funded station as "an assault tool of the hostile forces," and said its plans to begin broadcasts in Vietnamese were aimed at political sabotage.
Radio Free Asia began broadcasts to Burma on Feb. 4 and to Vietnam on Thursday, the eve of the Lunar New Year and start of the traditional Tet holiday.
The station, which was created by Congress, has been broadcasting in Mandarin Chinese and Tibetan for several months, and plans to extend its service to Cambodia, Laos and North Korea this year.
